## Why

This check closes the loop on two things. Your work has to be under version control from inside Positron. And your charter says the Positron transition is not finished until the settings portability decision is made.

You also have six checks' worth of miss-list entries. This is where each one gets resolved or accepted.

## What you will have at the end

- An ignore file that covers everything this repository should not track
- Every miss-list entry marked as solved, replaced, or still missing
- **The settings portability decision, made and written down**

**Time box:** 45 minutes. The R half is capped at 20.

## How to work this file

- Each task states an outcome. Finding the how is part of the check.
- Where a task asks you to predict, write the prediction before you test it.
- The hint names the Positron docs page to read if you get stuck. Use it only after trying.

## The decision: settings portability

Your charter requires this decision before the transition counts as complete.

**First, the facts.**

**How many machines will run Positron in the next 12 months?**

**Answer:**

**Find your user settings file on disk. What is its full path?**

**Answer:**

**Does Positron have a built-in way to sync settings between machines? Check, do not assume.**

**Answer:**

**Then, the options.**

| Option | What it is | Check before choosing |
|---|---|---|
| A | A settings-sync extension that stores settings, keybindings, snippets, and the extension list in a Git repository | Is it in Positron's Extensions view today? Does it work when you try it? |
| B | A private repository holding your settings, keybindings, and snippets files, linked into Positron's user folder on each machine | Do you know the user folder path on each machine? |
| C | Leave settings local | Is one machine really all you will use? |
